object_description: single-storey longitudinal school wing on the slope edge facing a large hall volume opposite
geometry_property: hall at the foot of the slope
design_condition: the hall is placed on the opposite slope as a vis-a-vis to the historic complex while the single-storey school wing frames the slope edge like a fine brushstroke, in analogy to the historic garden wall

positive: Placing the hall opposite creates a vis-a-vis to the castle complex and a counterpoint on the valley floor
Together with the pool and the outdoor fields, sporting activities can be concentrated
The single-storey school wing frames the unattractive slope edge naturally, in analogy to the historic garden wall
The conceptual approach of differentiating the two functions is interesting
The hall itself is well organised and well lit from two sides
The access level gives access to the hall and acts as a filter to the outdoor space with a canopy
The hall can therefore also be used attractively for festive events
The south facade with a large translucent photovoltaic shield stages the vis-a-vis architecturally
It promises a beautiful spatial atmosphere with reference to the landscape
The classrooms are well proportioned and can be used flexibly
Glazed or open inner partitions bring good sunlight into the depth of the plan
The outdoor spaces in front of the school are spacious and well sunlit despite their northern exposure
Hedges let them be experienced as islands in the open landscape
The parking design with hedges and chestnut trees is an appropriate response to the situation
The castle garden is enhanced and strengthened as a terrace with an unobstructed view
The glass shield, visible timber construction and concrete back correspond adequately to the concept
The pavilion building for the basic level is a pleasantly restrained timber construction
The all-weather pitch is sensibly positioned next to the gymnasium, leaving enough space for the grass fields
The daylight quotient is well achieved in both buildings
The elongated design ensures good flexibility of use for the basic level
negative: The intention of strengthening the landscape with this spatial focus cannot be achieved
Placing the very large hall volume at the foot of the slope is particularly unconvincing
The intrusion into the slope and the volumetric appearance disrupt the course of the slope in the open landscape
The formulation as an avalanche barrier seems sought-after
The psychomotor area on the upper floor is not possible here due to the distance to the classrooms
A spatially defined arrival or break area is missing for the school wing
The position of the gymnasium reinforces the existing incision in the sensitive topography
The garden design takes little account of the needs of the users
The narrow path connecting school building and existing complex is not convincing
Communal outdoor spaces at the entrance as a social meeting point are lacking
Overall the project is not compact enough
The energy standard can only be achieved with excessive effort, especially with the large north-facing glazing
The project exceeds the grey energy specification
The wooden facade is only partially protected by canopies
Despite the small floor area the split into two complex buildings makes it not cost-effective
The unfavourable building shape of the basic level is not economical
